attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-17
attempts.entry_title: Dentate gyrus place cells and memory discrimination (van Dijk and Fenton 2018)
attempts.summary: Some of the paper's main findings held up in this data, others did not, and the optogenetic silencing results could not be tested because those mice are not in the dataset. Dentate place cells were less stable than CA cells after wall removal, positional information rose before avoidances, and place cell-interneuron co-firing changed most after the shock zone moved, though this last rests on a guess at which sessions were compared. Place field counts fell short (CA single-field share 45% against 75%), likely because the paper does not define a place field. Avoidance learning and the correlation and network consistency changes near the shock zone did not reproduce. Minor table and control claims were mixed.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of van Dijk and Fenton (2018) on CRCNS hc-17, which holds the tetrode spike trains and tracking of wild-type mice in the environment manipulation experiment (45 DG and 20 CA place cells) and the active place avoidance task (42 DG place cells and 21 putative interneurons), with the paper's cell lists. It tests rate map stability and remapping, place field counts, positional information, overdispersion, network consistency and cell pair correlations. The optogenetic experiments of Figure 2 are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: Most place cells had a single place field in the first standard session (64% of DG and 75% of CA place cells), with no significant difference between the regions.
outcomes.source: Results, DG Place Field Remapping across a Modified Environment, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The majority of DG (64%) and CA (75%) place cells had a single place field during the initial recording in the standard environment (test of proportions, z = 1.6, p = 0.1)
outcomes.notes: Under every reading of the rate map (unsmoothed M2 a and b, the data set's smoothed maps, adopted, and our smoothing) and of the field rule (M5), the share of place cells with one field in the first standard session is 44 to 67% in DG and 35 to 55% in CA, against 64 and 75%; no reading puts both within tolerance, as CA stays below 67.5%. On the data set's smoothed maps few cells have no field (2 of 45 DG and 1 of 20 CA under M5 a); DG is 57.8% (M5 a) or 66.7% (M5 b), within tolerance, and CA 45.0 or 55.0%. The regions do not differ (p 0.34 to 0.68) except with our smoothing and M5 a (p = 0.042). Measured values are for the adopted smoothed maps with M5 a, the first M5 reading.
deviations: Rate maps use 32 x 32 bins of 8 tracker pixels, the grid of the data set's own maps (data/TIME, data/SPIKE, 1024 values; '_4' files with SCALE 8). The paper's 1.5 cm/pixel (STAR Methods, Recording set up) is about 1.4 cm in the arena and 2 cm in the environment boxes on this grid.

Place fields follow the claims file's M5 readings (at least 9 edge-contiguous bins above 20% of the peak, or above 1 AP/s), found on smoothed maps. M2 leaves smoothing open; the data set's own smoothed maps (RmSm), made by the authors and on the common grid for every environment session, are adopted, as the closest record of the maps the paper's fields were counted on. Unsmoothed maps (M2 a, b) and our 3 x 3 smoothing are shown. This replaces the unsmoothed maps of round 1, on which one-spike bins set the 20%-of-peak threshold (verifier, B1).
The first standard session of a day is its lowest-numbered circleintestbox session.

outcomes.statement: The number of place fields rose from the circular environments to the twice larger box after wall removal, more in DG (1.48 to 2.70) than in CA (1.19 to 2.0), with a condition effect, a region effect at p = 0.05 and no interaction; post hoc, removed DG exceeded circular DG and CA, and CA did not change.
outcomes.source: Results, DG Place Field Remapping across a Modified Environment, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The number of place fields scaled with the 2-fold increase in area from the circular (standard and cue-relocated environments) to the wall removal conditions, with the DG cells scaling more (DG circular, 1.48 ± 0.19 fields; removed, 2.70 ± 0.20 fields; CA circular, 1.19 ± 0.28 fields; removed, 2.0 ± 0.30 fields
outcomes.notes: On the data set's smoothed maps with M5 a, the adopted reading, mean fields per cell are 1.51 (DG circular), 2.09 (DG removed), 1.45 and 1.68 (CA), against 1.48, 2.70, 1.19 and 2.0. Three are within tolerance; removed DG is below 2.70 ± 0.39 under every reading (at most 2.09). Under the adopted reading the condition effect is p = 0.026 (cell as random term). Fisher's LSD with the mixed model's pooled error puts removed DG above circular DG (p = 0.0042) and above circular CA (p = 0.036), and circular and removed CA do not differ (p = 0.45), the paper's pattern; paired and unpaired t tests, the earlier post hoc test, put removed DG above circular DG (p = 0.011) but not above circular CA (p = 0.071). Across readings the pooled-error LSD puts removed DG above circular CA only with M5 a on smoothed maps (p = 0.036 and 0.024; elsewhere p 0.14 to 0.86). The outcome fails on the removed DG mean. Without the two sessions that fail the clock check the means are 1.50, 2.00, 1.45 and 1.61, condition p = 0.067.
deviations: Rate maps use 32 x 32 bins of 8 tracker pixels, the grid of the data set's own maps (data/TIME, data/SPIKE, 1024 values; '_4' files with SCALE 8). The paper's 1.5 cm/pixel (STAR Methods, Recording set up) is about 1.4 cm in the arena and 2 cm in the environment boxes on this grid.

Place fields follow the claims file's M5 readings (at least 9 edge-contiguous bins above 20% of the peak, or above 1 AP/s), found on smoothed maps. M2 leaves smoothing open; the data set's own smoothed maps (RmSm), made by the authors and on the common grid for every environment session, are adopted, as the closest record of the maps the paper's fields were counted on. Unsmoothed maps (M2 a, b) and our 3 x 3 smoothing are shown. This replaces the unsmoothed maps of round 1, on which one-spike bins set the 20%-of-peak threshold (verifier, B1).
Mixed models are statsmodels' REML linear mixed models with Wald F tests; their denominator df are not JMP's Kenward-Roger df (M12).

Fisher's LSD uses the pooled error of the mixed model with cell as random term (level means of the four region and condition groups and their covariance, residual df). Paired t tests within region and an unpaired t test across regions are shown beside it.

outcomes.statement: Rate map stability was lower in DG than in CA place cells, and lower for wall removal than for replication and cue relocation, with no region by manipulation interaction.
outcomes.source: Figure 1B; Results, DG Place Field Remapping across a Modified Environment, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Stability of place cells in Ammon's horn (CA) is higher than those in DG. Stability is lower for the removal manipulation than for replication and relocation manipulations
outcomes.notes: With one value per cell and manipulation (174 values), stability is higher in CA than in DG (mean z 0.42 against 0.31; region F = 8.73, p = 0.0036), differs by manipulation (F = 9.98, p = 0.0001), and Fisher's LSD puts removal below replication (p = 0.0001) and relocation (p = 0.0002); the interaction is p = 0.76 (paper 0.77). Reading (b) of M2 gives the same (region p = 0.0011, manipulation p = 0.0004). The data set gives 174 cell and manipulation values against the 178 the paper's df imply. Without the two sessions that fail the clock check (170 values) region p = 0.0034, manipulation p = 0.0004, LSD p = 0.0002 and 0.0008.
deviations: Rate maps use 32 x 32 bins of 8 tracker pixels, the grid of the data set's own maps (data/TIME, data/SPIKE, 1024 values; '_4' files with SCALE 8). The paper's 1.5 cm/pixel (STAR Methods, Recording set up) is about 1.4 cm in the arena and 2 cm in the environment boxes on this grid.

Every pair of sessions of a day of the paper's three conditions enters; diffcircle and transferbin sessions are left out, being none of the three versions. Stability is the maximum Pearson r over shifts of up to 2 bins, Fisher z (STAR Methods, Firing rate stability).
The environment session 140731_WT15_testbox2 duplicates testbox1 and is counted once.

outcomes.statement: The discharge properties of DG and CA place cells in the circular environment (waveform width, firing rate, short ISIs, coherence, information content, mean ISI, field number, theta phase) did not differ.
outcomes.source: Table S1; Results, DG Place Field Remapping across a Modified Environment, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: There are no differences in these characteristics between the regions
outcomes.notes: No property differs between DG and CA by ANOVA, Welch's ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis (smallest p 0.19). Firing rates (DG 0.95, CA 0.85 AP/s) are within tolerance. Information content is outside tolerance as bits per second (0.83 and 0.79 against 1.31 and 1.30) and within it as bits per spike (1.32 and 1.34), the variant; whether Table S1's bits/s is a mislabel is asked of a reader (questions/dijk-2018.yaml). Coherence (0.54 and 0.63) is outside 0.46 ± 0.06 and 0.51 ± 0.08. Field numbers on the data set's smoothed maps are 1.51 (DG) and 1.45 (CA), not different (p = 0.76). The mean ISI of the table (5.77 ms) is not what the files give for a mean ISI (3858 ms), so that row measures something else. Waveform width and theta phase cannot be computed, as the data set holds no waveforms or LFP.
deviations: Rate maps use 32 x 32 bins of 8 tracker pixels, the grid of the data set's own maps (data/TIME, data/SPIKE, 1024 values; '_4' files with SCALE 8). The paper's 1.5 cm/pixel (STAR Methods, Recording set up) is about 1.4 cm in the arena and 2 cm in the environment boxes on this grid.

Information content is Skaggs information on visited bins; coherence is Muller and Kubie's neighbour correlation, Fisher z, on unsmoothed maps (standard measures, as the paper names but does not define them).
Table S1 labels information content bits/s, but its values match bits per spike in these data; both are shown.

outcomes.statement: The recorded mice learned to avoid the shock zone in training 1 and kept the avoidance in training 2, while errors rose in the conflict trial and then fell.
outcomes.source: Figure 3B, top
outcomes.quote: mice learned to avoid in the first training trial and maintained avoidance memory during the second training trial. Errors in the conflict trial initially increased then quickly decreased
outcomes.notes: Errors fall from training 1 (mean 14.0) to training 2 (4.33) and rise in conflict (19.0), and paired comparisons put training 2 below training 1 (p = 0.028) and conflict (p = 0.042), but the criterion's test fails. The multivariate repeated-measures test whose df match the paper's (2, 4) gives F = 5.70, p = 0.067, against F = 18.2, p = 0.01. It also fails with WT15's 20-min training 2 file counted over its first 10 min (p = 0.067) and with WT15 left out (F(2, 3) = 3.37, p = 0.17). The univariate test, whose df do not fit six mice, gives F(2, 10) = 4.62, p = 0.038.
deviations: Errors are the Tracker's entrances in the shock-on files (avoidance state from 0 to 1). WT15 has no separate 10-min training 2 shock-on file; its 20-min file deposited among the shock-on files is used.
The criterion's reading (a), the multivariate test whose df (2, 4) match the paper's, decides; reading (b) is shown.
Variants for WT15, whose only training 2 file is 20 min long: its errors in the first 10 min, and the analysis without WT15.

outcomes.statement: Running speed did not differ between the training and conflict conditions.
outcomes.source: Results, DG-Dependent Memory Discrimination Is Not Selectively Accompanied by Dentate Firing Field Remapping, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: No differences in running speed were observed between the training and conflict conditions (F2,13 = 1.93, p = 0.18; data not shown)
outcomes.notes: Over training 1, training 2 and conflict in the shock-off recordings (5, 6 and 5 mice) the one-way ANOVA gives F(2, 13) = 1.94, p = 0.18, the paper's df and values. The shock-on sessions give p = 0.89. The readings with pretraining as a level differ (p = 0.0016 and 0.021), as mice run faster in pretraining (4.96 cm/s against 2.4 to 3.5).

outcomes.statement: Measures of spatial firing quality of DG place cells did not differ across pretraining, training and conflict.
outcomes.source: Results, DG-Dependent Memory Discrimination Is Not Selectively Accompanied by Dentate Firing Field Remapping, paragraph 2; Table S2

Room information is 1.15 and 0.73 bits/s in pretraining and conflict, outside the tolerance of 1.6 and 1.75; as bits per spike, the variant, it is 1.59 and 1.60, within it (asked of a reader, as for Table S1). Arena field counts differ on unsmoothed maps (p = 0.0018) and on the data set's smoothed maps (p = 0.0017), and room field counts on unsmoothed maps differ by Kruskal-Wallis (p = 0.030; ANOVA p = 0.091), but neither differs with our smoothing, the reading adopted for this task (room p = 0.42, arena p = 0.65).

Our 3 x 3 smoothing (weights 1, 0.5 and 0.25, the centred kernel closest to the authors' smoothed maps) is adopted in the place avoidance task, as four of its sessions have deposited maps on a 41 x 41 grid whose pixel mapping is not described, so the authors' maps cannot be used for every session of a mouse. Sessions the paper describes are missing. WT15, WT16 and WT19 have one pretraining session where the paper gives two, and WT16 has no training 1 recording. The paper's df (H2,117 and H2,435) imply values that need these sessions; the data give 115 place cell values and 428 place cell-interneuron changes.

The environment sessions 140731_WT15_testbox1 and 140731_WT15_testbox2 have the same position series, and three of the four listed units' spike trains begin with the same 20 spike times; two of the four listed units have identical trains, the other two differ in count (4371 against 4308 and 2615 against 2745 spikes), and the headers give different FIRST_TIMESTAMP values (11095 and 15235). They appear to be two sortings of one recording, and only one is counted. testbox1, the copy kept, fails the clock check (split-half map correlation no higher than with positions shifted by 60 s).

The Tracker files of the recordings of WT15 (after training 1 and 2) and WT16 (after training 2 and conflict) log a shock zone and 1 to 33 shocks with nonzero current, where the paper says recordings were made with the shock off. The WT15 training 2 recording is also deposited among the shock-on files (identical CRC), and WT16's conflict recording is named Conf1_1 in the TS files and Conf1_2 in its Tracker file. WT15's only training 2 Tracker file is 20 min long, where training 2 lasted 10 min, and holds one entrance.

For WT15, WT16 and WT19 the conflict shock zone (centre 305 degrees) is 170 degrees from the training zone (135 degrees), where the paper says the zone was relocated 180 degrees; for WT20, WT26 and WT27 it is 180.

The data descriptor says the Spike and Time maps hold 256 x 256 pixels written as one column; most hold 1024 values, a 32 x 32 grid of 8 tracker pixels, and the place avoidance maps of WT15Hab1, WT16Hab1, 150720_WT19Ini1_2 and 150720_WT19Conf1_2 hold 1681 values, a 41 x 41 grid whose mapping to tracker pixels is not stated and could not be recovered exactly. On the 32 x 32 grid a bin is about 1.4 cm in the arena and 2 cm in the environment boxes, where the paper gives 1.5 cm/pixel. The plain spike-count maps are close to, but not the same as, maps made from the TS files (median r 0.988 and 0.985).

The data set holds smoothed maps (files ending RmSm and ArSm) without a description of the smoothing (a least-squares fit shows it acts like a sum over about 2 x 2 bins, shifted by half a bin; the smoothed dwell time totals 4.5 times the plain one), and the TS file variants (Rm, Ar, _4, .times, 0spks, test-fix, and a misnamed file 151215_WT26Ini2_2_spikes_cl-fix.P1C1Rm151215_WT26Ini2_2_spikes_cl-fix.P1C1Rm) are not described; the meaning of each was inferred from the headers and by comparing files.
The WT19 pretraining session lasts 30 min, where the paper gives 20-min pretraining sessions. Environment sessions last 10, 20 or 30 min, which the paper does not state.

The files do not say how clusters were matched across the sessions of a day; the class lists give one entry per cell for the day, and this attempt assumes that a tetrode and cluster name is the same unit in every session.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The handover of the author run (executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed), the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier ran nothing from the notebook; it tested map_stability, place_fields, rm_multivariate, rm_univariate, ipos_series and coherence on synthetic inputs and read the archive listing for the blocked claims. Report in transcripts/dijk-2018/verifier-1-report.md. It disagrees with the record on one claim, fig3b-avoidance-learning.

disagreements.reason: Under the reading the df support (multivariate, F(2,4)), F = 5.70, p = 0.067; the paper has 18.2, p = 0.01 (cell 44). The univariate F(2,10) gives p = 0.038, but its df do not fit 6 mice. Also see B4.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the author-revise-1 run, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier ran nothing from the notebook; it read the new pooled-error LSD helper (mixed_lsd). Report in transcripts/dijk-2018/verifier-2-report.md. It agrees with all 44 outcomes. Text it found unsupported (the README's run time among it) was corrected and the outputs it asked for added in author-revise-2.

paper_notes.statement: Table S1 and Table S2 label information content in bits/s, but their values match Skaggs information in bits per spike computed from the files (DG 1.32 against 1.31; pretraining 1.59 against 1.6), not bits per second (0.83 and 1.15). The mean ISI of the tables (5 to 6 ms) is not the mean interspike interval of these cells (seconds).

The paper does not define a place field or say whether its rate maps were smoothed. On unsmoothed maps with the claims file's field rules many cells have no field. On the authors' deposited smoothed maps few have none and three of the four field means of Figure 1 are within tolerance, but the single-field share of CA cells (45 to 55% against 75%) and the field count of removed DG cells (2.09 against 2.70) stay below the paper's. Question for the authors, which smoothing and which field rule (threshold, minimum size, contiguity) were used, and were the deposited RmSm and ArSm maps the ones analysed?

The paper does not say which session pairs form the shock addition and shock relocation comparisons. This attempt adopts every pretraining-training pair for addition and both training sessions against conflict for relocation; several outcomes (fig3d whole-cell, fig5d2, figs2bc at 20 ms, fig5d3, the Figure 6 rate change insets) hold under this reading and not under the adjacent-session reading. Question for the authors, which pairs were used?

The size of location x in Ipos is not stated; Figure 4B and the Figure 4D map correlation hold with 8-pixel bins and not with 16-pixel blocks. The 5-s episodes of overdispersion and network consistency, the meaning of overlapping firing fields, and the statistical criteria classing place cell-interneuron pairs as positive, negative or independent are not stated either. Questions for the authors, the location size, whether episodes tile the session or follow field entries, and the test used to class pairs (the Kruskal-Wallis df for the classes imply more values than pairs times manipulations).

entries.name: dijk-2018
entries.title: Dentate gyrus place cells and memory discrimination (van Dijk and Fenton 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of van Dijk and Fenton (2018) on CRCNS hc-17, which holds the tetrode spike trains and tracking of wild-type mice in the environment manipulation experiment (45 DG and 20 CA place cells) and the active place avoidance task (42 DG place cells and 21 putative interneurons), with the paper's cell lists. It tests rate map stability and remapping, place field counts, positional information, overdispersion, network consistency and cell pair correlations. The optogenetic experiments of Figure 2 are not in the data set.
